title: Cold rebuild: hash and verify passwords
summary: Rebuild HashPassword and VerifyPassword from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: You wrote **HashPassword** and **VerifyPassword** in *Session fixation and password storage*. Write them again from an
**empty editor**. The tests are the ones you passed: the stored format, a random salt, the stored iteration count,
and malformed input that must return false.
If you get stuck, go back to the lesson and try again tomorrow. This check, plus the boss, proves the module.

steps.prompt: Why is the iteration count stored next to the hash?
options: So the cost can be raised later while old hashes still verify (and can be upgraded at the next sign-in)
Because the salt is derived from it
It is not needed: PBKDF2 always uses 600,000

steps.title: Rebuild the password functions cold
prompt: Write `string HashPassword(string password)` returning `pbkdf2-sha256$600000$<Base64 salt>$<Base64 hash>` (16-byte random salt, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 32-byte hash), and `bool VerifyPassword(string password, string stored)` that uses the stored iterations and salt, compares in constant time, and returns `false` for anything malformed. `using System.Security.Cryptography;`.
